newsitem.title: UK: WH Smith chief quits to join BT.
newsitem.headline: WH Smith chief quits to join BT.

text.p: British retailer W.H. Smith Group Plc said on Monday chief executive Bill Cockburn will leave the company in October to become group managing director at British Telecommunications Plc

The group also said that its results for the year to May 31, 1997 would be within the range of market expectations and would show benefits from its recovery programme which began last year. Sales in the second half were up six percent overall and up three percent based on comparable stores.
Cockburn, who joined the group in November 1995, will continue as chief executive until he leaves in October, Smith said in a statement.

Chairman Jeremy Hardie said that Cockburn had been a catalyst for change within the group, presiding over the sale of several of Smith's non-core businesses, notably Do It All home improvement stores and Business Supplies.

Cockburn said in the statement he had started an unprecedented programme of change throughout the group. "Normally I would have wanted to see my plans through to fruition. My decision to join BT was not taken lightly but it is the chance of a lifetime for me."

Cockburn was brought in to shake up the struggling retailer, which last year reported its first ever loss in its 200 year history. Smith has found life increasingly tough as food superstores began encroaching on the natural territory of its core chain, which sells newspapers, magazines, books, greeting cards, stationery, videos and recorded music.
